content.overview: Chapter V (from s. 63) sits before offences against the human body. Rape is s. 63 (definition) and s. 64 (punishment). s. 69 is the new deceitful-sexual-intercourse offence. IPC 377 is not re-enacted.

content.study:
Topic at a glance
Sexual offences are a current-law Chapter, not a copy of the 2013 IPC package with new numbers. Some sections map; s. 69 does not.

Core map
s. 63 — rape (old 375). The marital-rape exception remains in the statute; Independent Thought read it down for wives under 18. Do not write that marital rape of an adult wife is an offence unless a later Constitution Bench so holds — current-law honesty matters.
s. 64 — punishment (old 376).
s. 69 — sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means, including false promise of marriage. New. Do not map it onto s. 63.
s. 70 — gang rape. Gang rape of a woman under 18 can carry remainder-of-life or death — quote the Bare Act in the exam.

Consent
Consent must be unequivocal, voluntary, and capable of being withdrawn. Tukaram is the cautionary tale of how not to try a rape case. The 2013 statutory definition of consent is now in this Chapter — confirm the exact BNS clause rather than reciting IPC 375 sixthly from memory.

Child
[[REF:DEFINITION:CRIMINAL-LAW:CHILD]] is below 18 throughout. POCSO continues to apply on its own terms for sexual offences against children; do not pretend the BNS repealed POCSO.

IPC 377
Not re-enacted. Navtej remains the constitutional holding on consensual same-sex intimacy. Non-consensual male rape is a legislative gap in the BNS text — do not invent a section.

Current-law position
Cite 63/64, not 375/376, for offences on or after 1 July 2024.

Educational note
This is original CodePackr teaching. Confirm punishments in India Code before a sentencing answer.

provisions.title: Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means

examples.title: Example 1 — simple
examples.body: A obtains sexual intercourse by a promise of marriage he never intended to keep. That is the s. 69 fact pattern. Whether it is also s. 63 depends on whether consent under s. 63 is vitiated — do not collapse the two sections automatically.

examples.title: Example 2 — legal
examples.body: Two or more persons acting in furtherance of common intention commit rape. Charge s. 70, not only s. 64 read with s. 3(5).

hypotheticals.question: Does the exception apply?
hypotheticals.analysis: Independent Thought read down the marital-rape exception so that it does not apply to a wife below 18. A 17-year-old wife is a child. The exception, as read down, does not protect A. (Adult-wife marital rape remains a different, unsettled statutory question — do not invent a holding.)

rows.left: Sexual intercourse without consent as defined
rows.right: Sexual intercourse by deceitful means (including false promise of marriage)

misconceptions.correction: s. 63 is the rape definition. s. 69 is a separate new offence.
It is not re-enacted. Navtej already read down 377 for consensual adult same-sex intimacy.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are the BNS sections for definition and punishment of rape?
Which BNS section covers sexual intercourse by deceitful means?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: s. 69 — a new offence, not a clone of s. 63.

cases.name: Independent Thought v. Union of India
cases.holding: The marital-rape exception does not apply to a wife below 18.
cases.relevance: Must be cited whenever the exception is mentioned.

cases.name: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
cases.holding: Consensual same-sex intimacy between adults is not an offence. IPC 377 was read down; the BNS does not re-enact 377.
cases.relevance: Do not charge a BNS 377. There is none.

cases.name: Tukaram v. State of Maharashtra
cases.holding: The Mathura case — a cautionary tale on consent and the treatment of the prosecutrix. Use it as history of why the consent definition was recast, not as current good law on consent.
cases.relevance: History / reform, not the rule you apply today.

examFrameworks.question: Explain rape under the BNS.
steps: Do not write 375/376 as current law.

examFrameworks.question: Discuss sexual offences in Chapter V BNS, including s. 69 and the fate of IPC 377.
steps: s. 69 as a new offence, distinguished from rape.
Independent Thought; Navtej; Tukaram as history.

examTips: If the facts are a false promise of marriage, start with s. 69, then ask whether s. 63 is also made out. Do not skip 69.
